subject: koala
reasoning:
I'm planning a rigged koala model as a single module, aiming for a compact but well-proportioned build with a seated pose, leaning torso, and legs positioned naturally for sitting.

Working out the joint coordinates for hips, spine, chest, neck, and head, then setting up a spine chain with tapered radii so the body sweeps smoothly from hips to head, and adjusting hip height so the belly sits just above the floor.

For the head, I'm placing it wide and slightly flattened on a sphere scaled for a koala's broad face, with a dark oval nose sphere positioned toward the front.

Planning the jaw as a separate parented part below the head for mouth movement, with big flat fluffy ears made of outer grey and inner cream spheres, plus small black eye spheres positioned symmetrically on the face.

Now I'm checking that eyes and nose sit on the head's ellipsoid surface by computing distances from the head center, adjusting positions slightly so they sink naturally into the rounded shape rather than floating outside it. Next I'm moving on to placing the shoulders and arms.

Adding paw and finger joints...

Still working out finger positions...

Now moving to the legs: hips seated with thighs going forward and shins angling down to planted feet, working out approximate joint coordinates for hip, knee, and ankle with a thigh radius around 0.07.

Continuing the leg chain down to ankle, foot, and toes with claws touching the floor, defining sweep radii that taper from hip to ankle, and naming each joint per side (L/R) for the skeletal chain.

For the cream chest patch, I'm positioning an ellipsoid near the front of the chest so it protrudes slightly beyond the body surface, attached to the nearest spine bone. I'm also adding small cream spheres at the cheeks for fluffy tuft accents and considering cream fringe on the ears, while skipping a rump patch for now.

Now I'm layering a mottled grey pattern over the body and head using a paint function, then applying a countershade effect with cream tones to darken the underside relative to the top. For the skeleton, I'm setting up a head joint branching from the spine tip with aim direction angled slightly forward and up, plus a jaw joint positioned a bit below and ahead of it.

Working out jaw and ear placement...

Still defining ear geometry and colors...

For the coat I'm applying a mottled countershading effect blending grey with cream tones, softened at the edges. For the spine, I'm setting up a chain of joints along a catmull-rom path with four control points, then sweeping the skin mesh along that chain with varying radii at each joint.

Legs branch off the hips root, and arms branch off the third spine joint near shoulder height. I'm naming each finger segment with side and index identifiers, parenting them to the arm chain tip, then attaching claw spikes and rod-shaped finger bones with appropriate colors...

Switching to a sweep along the finger chain for rounded caps, and using capsule shapes bound to the leg tip for the toes.
